questions.q: What is the first step toward paying for your dreams, according to Kobliner?
a: Work out what they cost and review your spending
Take out a loan for the full amount
Wait until your income rises
Ask family for a down payment
questions.why: The first lesson says to price the dream, then plan how your finances can get you there.

questions.q: For a $20,000 car, how much down payment does the summary mention?
a: About $4,000
About $2,000
About $10,000
About $500
questions.why: The first lesson uses a 20% down payment to show how a big goal becomes a concrete plan.

questions.q: What does the $3,500 credit card example show about minimum payments?
a: They can keep you paying for decades
They clear the balance within five years
They usually keep interest under 5%
They save money compared with paying early
questions.why: The second lesson says minimum payments at 17% interest could last until age 65.

questions.q: What should you do if you are already stuck in credit card debt?
a: Ask lenders for a lower rate and see a non-profit counselor
Open more cards and spread the balance
Stop paying until the lender negotiates
Borrow from retirement savings first
questions.why: The second lesson suggests negotiating with lenders and using savings, since card interest beats investment returns.

questions.q: Why is it worth comparing several insurance quotes?
a: The same policy can cost wildly different amounts
Insurers are required by law to match prices
Cheaper policies always cover much less
Employers negotiate the best available rates
questions.why: The third lesson cites one young man who could pay anywhere from $808 to $3,441 for identical car cover.
